request.spec:
A button downloads the policy versions as a CSV file: a header line
version,from,key,value,claims,due-total then one line per version with its claims' count and the
due of those that count, added up.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A button downloads the policy versions as a CSV file: a header line
version,from,key,value,claims,due-total then one line per version with its claims' count and the
due of those that count, added up.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I added an "Export policy versions (CSV)" button, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

The file starts with the header line `version,from,key,value,claims,due-total`, then has one line per policy version, oldest first. A claim belongs to the version in force on its date. Deleted claims and claims dated before the first version aren't counted in any line. The due-total adds up each counted claim's due as its row on screen shows it, skipping any shown as "n/a".

**What changed:**
- **Server:** `SettingsResponse.java` now also sends each version in full (number, from-date, key, value). It uses the existing `Settings.policyVersionList`, so values look the same as in the existing policy-versions list (`3.00`, `5`, and so on).
- **Front end:** the new button is in `features/export/exportPolicy.slot.tsx` and has the `data-testid` `export-policy`. Like the other export buttons, it stays disabled until the sheet's data has finished loading. `useSettings.ts` has the matching new type.

Two choices the request didn't settle:
- A version with no from-date (in force on every date) gets an empty `from` cell, not the word "start" that the on-screen list uses.
- The due is worked out in the browser, the same way the claims and periods exports do it, so it always matches what the claim rows show.

probe.probe_text:
I changed nothing. Below is what the code does, with the code's own names. Where the code and its comments disagree, I say so. ## 1. Figures and the rules behind them ### Claim row (`claims.slot.tsx` → `PersonClaims`) | Shown (`data-testid`) | Where it comes from / rule | |---|---| | `claim-amount`, `claim-date`, `claim-note`, `claim-ref`, `claim-tags` | Stored values. A claim with lines takes its amount from them, added up (`ClaimLines`), and you can't type another amount. A negative amount is a **correction** (`isCorrection`): it must name, in `corrects`, a SETTLED claim of the same person, and it can't go beyond `Claims.remaining`. | | `claim-due` | `claimDueCents` in the browser, `Figures.due` on the server. It is the fixed `due` if the claim is settled. Otherwise it is `statedDue` if a statement binds it. Otherwise it is **live**: amount × rate ÷ 100, raised to the `floor` in force on the claim's date, plus `charge`. A correction gets no floor and no charge. No rate gives `n/a`. | | rate | `Rates.pct` / `claimRateOn` uses the grade the person had on the claim's date (`gradeOn`) and the rate in force on that date. Rates fall back to parent sheets up to 3 levels up (`PARENT_LEVELS`), then to the sheet it was cloned from (`lineage`). A rate saved with a from-date on or after today is **forward-only** (`forwardAfter`): it applies only to claims with a higher `seq`. A rate past its `to`-date is no rate. | | rounding / `halfUp` | `Figures.rounding`: the sheet's dated `rounding` setting in force on the claim's date if one is set. Otherwise HALF_UP for a claim dated before `policyDate` (which defaults to the sheet's today) and HALF_EVEN on or after it. A correction rounds by the date of the claim it corrects (`roundingDate`). | | late charge | `Figures.charge` / `lateChargeCents`. The claim must be OPEN or PENDING, not deferred, not waived and not a correction. For every full 30 days past `overdueFrom` (`dueBy` + `grace` for the grade on the claim's date), it adds the `late-pct` in force on that boundary date. It compounds, and each step is rounded. It follows the sheet's today. | | `claim-due-by` | Fixed when the claim is added (`DueBy.of`): the terms-th business day after the claim's date, skipping weekends and holidays. Terms are the person's own, else their grade's, else the sheet's (default 14), all looked up on the **sheet's today**. Re-dating the claim leaves it alone. A new holiday on or before it re-fixes it (`RefixDueBys`, not for SETTLED or VOID claims). A steward can set it directly (`ApplyClaimDueBySet`); it then keeps no terms and is never re-fixed. | | `claim-overdue` | `overdue`: OPEN or PENDING, not deferred, and `dueBy` + grace is before today. | | `claim-period` | The period whose dates contain the `dueBy` (`periodOf`). | | `claim-number` | Given at **settle or approve** (`ClaimNumbers.next`). If period numbering is on, it is `-n`, or `X-n` when no period contains the due-by. Otherwise it is `FY-n` by the fiscal year of the due-by. A voided claim keeps its number, and numbers are never reused. | | `claim-status` | DRAFT, REVIEW, OPEN, PENDING, SETTLED, VOID, DELETED. `ClaimStatus.counts()` is true for OPEN, PENDING and SETTLED. `isOpen()` is true for OPEN and PENDING. | | `claim-stated` | A statement binds the claim. | | `claim-deferred`, `claim-deferred-until` | Deferred while today is before `deferredUntil` and no statement binds the claim. A deferred claim is in no total, is not overdue and can't be settled. | | `claim-policy` | `usePolicyVersions().on(date)`: how many policy versions have a from-date on or before the claim's date. | | `claim-review-late`, `claim-pending-late` | The day the claim went to REVIEW or PENDING (from its log), plus `reviewSla` or `pendingSla` days, is before today. | | `claim-opened-by`, `claim-batch`, `claim-split-from`, `claim-late-entry`, `claim-reminded`, `claim-waived`, `claim-held`, `claim-review-assigned`, `claim-proofs` (+ receipt/photo), `claim-log`, `claim-comments`, `claim-lines`, `claim-shares` | Stored values. `lateEntry` means the claim was added into a soft-closed period. Reminding is once per sheet-today, and escalates once if `escalateAfter` is set. `held` is display only. | ### Person row | Shown | Rule | |---|---| | `person-claimed` | Sum of `amount` over claims that pass `claimedLive` / `countsClaimed`. Counts: OPEN, PENDING and SETTLED; not deferred; not an open claim once `retiredOut` (today has reached the retirement date) unless stated. Corrections are left out. | | `person-due-total` | `personDueCents` (browser) / `Rollup.snapshot` (server). It adds the counting claims' dues, less the parts held by people the claims are shared with (`carriedCents` / `Figures.part`), plus this person's parts of claims shared with them. It is `n/a` if there is no rate today and no claim has a figure. It is capped by `capCents` / `Settings.capped`: at most the `cap` in force on the date of the person's latest counting claim, minus their pool `cut` total, never below 0. | | `person-excess` | `excessCents`: how far due-total plus cut is over the cap. | | `person-settled-total`, `person-open-total` | The due-total before the cap, split into SETTLED claims and OPEN/PENDING claims. | | `person-overdue-count`, `person-overdue-total` | `overdueFigures` over the person's own live claims. | | `person-score`, `person-band` | `scoreOf`: settled figures (corrections left out) ÷ 100, minus 5 per overdue claim, rounded HALF_EVEN. Band is HIGH or MID or LOW against `scoreHigh` and `scoreMid`, shown only while both are set. | | `person-grade`, `person-terms`, `person-name` | `gradeOn(today)`; their own terms in force today. | | `person-period-

-due-total`, `-carried` | `personPeriodDueCents` / `personPeriodCarriedCents`, live until the period is closed. | | `person-aged-0-30/31-60/61` | Dues of their live OPEN/PENDING claims, bucketed by the claim's age. Not capped. | | `person-active` | They have an OPEN or PENDING claim that counts, dated in the last 30 days. | | `person-backing` | Patrons' SETTLED fixed dues over the last 90 days × each patron's share, rounded HALF_EVEN. | | `person-cut-total` | Pool cuts. A person with a hold in force today gets no cut; a retired member is left out. | | `person-claims-OPEN/SETTLED-count`, statement count/total/date, snapshots, flag, approver, retired, holds | Stored values. | ### Sheet totals (`useSheetTotals`, and `Rollup` for the audit) - `claimedTotal` is a plain sum. - `dueTotal`, `overdueTotal`, `settledTotal`, `openTotal` and `cutTotal` are `trimmedTotal`: skip `n/a`, and with 3 or more figures leave out the single highest and lowest. - The server's `Rollup.record` writes the ROLLUP, TOTALS and ALERT audit lines (ALERT uses `alertThreshold`). ### What freezes, and when - **Settle or approve** freezes `due` at the figure then, late charge and floor included, or at the as-of date's figure when settled as of a date. Shares' parts freeze with it (`partOf`). - **Re-settle** (steward only) freezes it again at today's unbound figure. - **A statement** (`TakeStatement`) binds every counting claim to its due as shown, including SETTLED ones; every other claim is unbound. It records `statedTotal`. Cancelling it (steward only) unbinds the claims, and an earlier statement's figures are not restored. Reassigning or splitting a claim also unbinds it. - **Closing a period** (`PeriodCloser`) fixes, for claims due by in it, each person's total and carried figure (which includes their opening balance) and the pool cuts. Claims count by their status at the end of the period's last day, taken from the log. - **Closed:** a claim due by in it can't be added, edited, opened, settled, voided, proved, deferred, re-dated or reassigned (`ClosedPeriods.refuse`). - **Soft-closed:** figures are fixed but claims can still change, and new ones are late entries. - **Locked:** can't be reopened. - A **period `cap`** limits each person's OPEN or PENDING claims in the period. - **Auto-close** on a today change happens when the period's to-date + `graceDays` is before the new today. Rollover soft-closes the old year. - **A change of today** writes SNAPSHOT lines (and SCORE lines if `scoreLog` is on), releases every editor lock, and runs the auto-close. ### Who may do what - **Permission matrix** (`Settings.allows`): - By default, any role except viewer may open, settle, void, close and change today. That includes `restricted`. - Reassign and reopen need a steward. - A viewer can change nothing (`ViewerGuard`; bulk actions still answer, with nothing done). - Nothing changes on an archived sheet. - A delegation in force today makes the user a steward. - **Steward only:** void a SETTLED claim within 7 days of settling; approve PENDING (the person's `approver` may too); review REVIEW; re-date; set due-by; waive; re-settle; assign a review; flag; merge or undo a merge; transfer; cancel a statement; lock or unlock a period; roll over. Only a steward can open a claim of a **flagged** person. - **Four-eyes:** whoever opened or last edited a claim can't settle or approve it. For a part-settle, this is judged on the original claim. - **Clerk limit:** a clerk or restricted user settling a claim whose due is over the clerk limit (the grade's, else the sheet's) sends it to PENDING. - **Thresholds and limits:** - over `proofThreshold` (the grade's, else the sheet's): it needs a proof, or one of each `proofKinds`, before settle or approve; - over `noteThreshold`: it needs a note to open; - over `reviewThreshold`: opening sends it to REVIEW; - `maxOpen`: per-person limit on open claims. - A void needs a reason from the sheet's list while that list isn't empty. - A DELETED claim can be restored only on the same sheet-today it was deleted. - No claim can be dated after the person's retirement date, or inside a past retirement. ### Holds and imports - **Hold:** in code, neither a claim hold nor a person hold changes any figure (`Person.counts`, `heldOn` → only `retiredOut`). A person hold only removes that person's pool cut. - **Import people:** a line matching an existing name or alias edits that person; any other line adds one. A blank grade takes `defaultGrade`. - **Paste claims:** a line matching an existing claim's date and note updates the newest such DRAFT; otherwise it adds a claim. Every pasted claim is then opened. - **Import openings:** adds to the person's opening balance for the period, which goes into their carried figure. - **Import rates:** works as the rate form does, so forward-only rules apply. - Each import, and the paste, is all-or-nothing. ### Where the code and its comments disagree - **Holds:** several comments still say a hold takes claims out of totals. That includes `ClaimStatus.isOpen`, the browser's `isOpen` and `Claim.held`, the `usePeople` header, `PeriodCloser`, `TakeStatement`, and an inline comment in `PersonClaims`. The code does not do this. - **PENDING claims:** the `PersonClaims` header says a PENDING claim shows its live figure, not its bound one. The code (`Figures.figure`) shows the bound figure. - **Clerk limit date:** the `ApplyClaimStatus` javadoc says the limit is the one "on the sheet's today". The code uses the claim's date. - **When a claim is numbered:** the browser's `Claim.number` comment says "when opened" and the `PersonClaims` header says a split-off claim gets "the next number". The code numbers a claim only when it is settled. - **Due-by terms:** `Claim.getDueBy` says the terms come from the grade on the claim's date. `DueBy.terms` uses the person's own terms, else the grade's, else the sheet's, all on the sheet's today. - **Smaller oddities:** `TakeStatement.work` computes a total it almost always throws away. `countsClaimed` is an exact copy of `counts`. ## 2. How hard it was to follow The logic is scattered and tangled: the core figure math is written twice, once in Java (`Figures`, `Rollup`, `Person.counts`, `Settings`) and once in TypeScript (`useClaims.ts`, `useRates.ts`, `useSheetTotals.ts`, `usePeriods.ts`, and repeated inside `claims.slot.tsx`). The permission and freeze rules are spread over about 60 single-step classes, and the long comments, which are the main guide, are stale in several places, so a new developer can't trust them without checking each rule in both languages.
